openings.claim: Change the yokes into rim-supported guide bridges: lateral stops register the hatch while a small roof clearance permits vertical accommodation of the disturbed contact.
openings.delta: Use the four strips as two removable bolted pairs only if their geometry permits padded clamping onto the rim with upper strips overlapping hatch edges. Route clamp force through the rim, leaving the hatch outside that compression path. Use a supplied 1 mm card temporarily to gauge roof clearance, then remove it. Bolt shafts provide opposing lateral stops. Cord retains removable hardware; withdraw both bridges fully onto the tabletop for inspection.
openings.prediction: The nearest rival is the prior lightly compressed registered yoke. If compression coupling causes the observed corner lift, rim-supported clearance should reduce opposite-corner lift during the right-card trial while retaining lateral registration. If either construction rocks equally, or clearance permits displacement over 1 mm, the proposed bypass loses its advantage. This is an unmeasured hypothesis.
openings.probe: First inspect geometry without loading. Allocate two closure/pull trials to the prior yoke, one centered and one disturbed; allocate ten to ten successive opening cycles of the guide bridge, with the final closure disturbed. Record ruler displacement and corner lift, stopwatch reopening time, and seal tears. Compare disturbed results, then assess all ten bridge cycles against the valued outcome. Twelve trials and two configurations are the complete allowance; no repeat or rival durability inference.
assumptions: Rim underside access, strip reach, bolt length and contact elevations are indispensable unknowns. Reject if the supplied parts cannot establish independent rim bearing and roof clearance without altering original parts.
Lateral stop spacing must allow closure yet limit movement to 1 mm; unsuitable bolt diameters or geometry defeat the construction.
Roof clearance may weaken retention, bind during disturbed closure or permit rocking; pads may slip or mark the seal. Reject damage or unmet outcomes.
Fabrication must fit ninety minutes, readings twenty minutes, and each reopening thirty seconds; these capacities are unverified.

assessment: A geometry-dependent probe, not deployment. Separate rim support may accommodate the disturbance; no feasibility or performance has been established.

lineage.reason: Retains removable lateral registration but changes the compression carrier to the rim and introduces gauged vertical clearance.
